For 2026/27: 1 February 2026 (undergraduate applicants from North America); 28 February 2026 (undergraduate and graduate taught applicants from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan, and graduate taught applicants from South Asia); 31 March 2026 (all other undergraduate and graduate taught applicants). The page states the 2027/28 dates are still to be confirmed and details will be available by early November.

official.description: UCD offers a limited number of Global Excellence Scholarships of 100% and 50% of the tuition fee to outstanding international students on non-EU fees who are starting undergraduate or graduate taught programmes in September. Applicants must already hold an offer or conditional offer on an eligible course, and the award is not automatically renewed.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a two-stage race: UCD will not consider you for the scholarship until you already hold an offer or conditional offer on an eligible programme, so the programme application is the real deadline. Because UCD warns about a significant surge in applications and processing delays during peak scholarship competition windows, an application filed in the final days before a regional deadline is the most common way to be shut out. Budget your own money for everything except tuition: the award is a fee waiver only, and UCD publishes no stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EU-fee applicants who apply early to an eligible UCD undergraduate or graduate taught programme and can fund Irish living costs themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm fee classification early using UCD's fees page, because only students classed as non-EU qualify
Check your exact programme against the Eligible Programmes 2026 document before doing anything else; a popular programme that is excluded wastes the whole effort
File the programme application months ahead of your regional deadline so an offer or conditional offer is in hand in time
Download and read the Terms & Conditions 2026/27 and Application Instructions 2026 as soon as the 2027/28 versions appear in early November
Diarise the regional deadline that applies to your region, not the latest date on the list
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that is absent from the Eligible Programmes list
Leaving the programme application so late that no offer exists when the scholarship deadline passes
Assuming the scholarship renews itself; continuing students are reassessed and notified only between late September and October
Missing that results come via SISWeb roughly seven weeks after the regional deadline, so inquiries before then get no answer
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: UCD publishes no stipend, so Dublin accommodation, living costs, insurance and travel remain entirely on the applicant.
document_audit: The official page defers all document rules to the separate Application Instructions 2026 PDF, so do not rely on the scholarship page's FAQ for the document list
The Terms & Conditions 2026/27 are published as a linked PDF on a third-party document host; open them directly rather than relying on a summary
Eligible Programmes 2026 is a separate linked document and is the only authoritative source for whether your course qualifies
Your region assignment determines your deadline, so check the geographic wording carefully if you studied or reside somewhere other than your home country
alerts: The 2027/28 round had not opened when checked: UCD says applications open in November with dates TBC, so an applicant who waits for the old February dates will miss the window
The 2026/27 deadlines differed by up to two months by region, so a single 'UCD deadline' in a listing is misleading
No award is automatic; the scholarship depends on securing an eligible-programme offer first, which means admission processing time is the hidden constraint
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme application first, then a separate scholarship application in line with UCD's Application Instructions 2026 once an offer or conditional offer exists.
